requirement: Every resource access must verify that the requesting user is authorized to access that specific resource (ownership/authorization check).
prohibited: Returning a resource purely because a valid ID was supplied, without checking ownership.
remediation: Add a server-side ownership/authorization check before returning the resource.

requirement: Never trust an identity or object ID supplied directly by the client as the sole basis for access.
prohibited: Deriving the acting user's identity from a client-supplied field (e.g. a body/query parameter) rather than the authenticated session/token.
good_example: user_id = current_user.id  # derived from the verified session/token
remediation: Derive the acting user's identity from the authenticated session/access token, not from client input.

requirement: Authorization checks must be performed server-side; client-side checks (hidden fields, disabled buttons) are not sufficient.
prohibited: Relying on frontend/Angular UI restrictions as the only access control.
bad_example: // Angular hides the delete button, but the DELETE endpoint has no server-side check
good_example: // DELETE endpoint independently verifies the caller owns/administers the resource
remediation: Add the equivalent server-side authorization check regardless of what the UI already restricts.

requirement: Changing a resource identifier in a request (e.g. /user/123 -> /user/124) must not expose another user's data.
prohibited: Sequential/guessable resource IDs served without a per-request authorization check.
bad_example: GET /user/124  # returns user 124's private data to user 123's session
good_example: GET /user/124  # returns 403 because the session belongs to user 123
remediation: Verify object ownership on every request, independent of how the ID was obtained.
